purpose: Evaluate the preregistered cap-28 cue-width hypothesis on its two named, previously inspected Qb3 development probes using the same informative-minus-absent score contrast as the audited cap-14 comparison.
scope: Read-only all-legal neural assessment after the completed and audited cap-28 training run. These probes are development data, not independent transfer or final-test evidence. No training or memory updates occur.
metric: For each legal move, score-change is the condition's final absolute MBON score minus the absent-control absolute score on the same board/action under the same encoder cap. Rank descending with lexical UCI tie-break. For informative memory, both success moves must rank strictly better (smaller rank) than their recorded cap-14 rank for the cap-increase hypothesis to pass. Shuffled-minus-absent and disabled-minus-absent ranks are reported as controls, not substituted for the informative criterion.
falsification: The cap-increase prediction fails if either informative success-move rank is not strictly better than its cap-14 rank, if matched control exposure/audit fails, if exact total cue current is not 21 with 28 active cells at 0.75 each, or if required certificate/provenance checks fail.
